key_terms.الشَّهَادَةِ: testimony (shahada) — the act of bearing witness or testifying in legal proceedings
key_terms.الشُّهَدَاءُ: witnesses (shuhada) — those who have observed an event and can testify in legal proceedings; in Quranic context, those required to witness contracts and transactions
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic (Azza wa-Jalla) — an honorific formula used when mentioning Allah

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the Quranic verse 2:282 regarding witnesses being summoned?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the Quranic verse 2:282 which commands witnesses not to refuse when summoned. The Imam clarifies that this obligation applies specifically before the testimony is given — meaning witnesses must present themselves when called upon to testify, not after the act of testifying. This ruling was significant in early Islamic jurisprudence as it established the duty of witnesses to appear when required by those seeking legal documentation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:282]
and the witnesses should not refuse when they are summoned.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has narrated the following: “This is about the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious. ‘
. . . the witnesses must not refuse to testify when they are summoned to testify,’ [2:282]
abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, has said, ‘It is before the presentation of testimony.’”
